slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
To map one figure onto a congruent copy, describe a sequence of rigid motions. One reliable method: translate so one vertex lands on its partner, rotate about that vertex so a second vertex lines up, then reflect across that side if the third vertex is on the wrong side.

So any two congruent figures are related by at most three motions of this kind. Every rigid motion of the plane is in fact a composition of at most three reflections.

slides.html: Triangle ABC has the opposite orientation from its congruent partner. Must a reflection be in the sequence?
slides.reveal: Yes. Translations and rotations keep orientation; only a reflection (an odd number of them) reverses it.
